bull.b: Very low leverage gives Oculis greater financial flexibility than a heavily indebted development-stage biotech. The modest debt burden reduces near-term balance-sheet pressure and leaves more capacity to direct capital toward clinical programs, regulatory work, and other strategic priorities.

The return from negative equity to a substantial positive equity base indicates meaningful balance-sheet repair over time. Although operations remain loss-making, this stronger capital position provides a more resilient foundation for funding development activities and managing future financing needs.

Acquiring full rights can give Oculis greater control over development, regulatory strategy, and eventual commercialization of these assets. The transaction also supports the company’s neuro-ophthalmology strategy and may improve long-term economics by replacing prior obligations to its licensor.

bear.b: Sustained cash consumption of this magnitude means Oculis must continue funding clinical development without meaningful operating cash generation. External financing dependence can constrain strategic flexibility and may require additional capital before the pipeline produces commercial or partnership revenue.

The company currently lacks a meaningful recurring revenue base, leaving financial performance dependent on future clinical and regulatory progress. The sharp revenue decline reinforces that Oculis remains pre-commercial and has limited internal resources to offset research and development spending.

The ATM facility increases financing flexibility, but issuing shares would dilute existing ownership and could pressure per-share participation in future pipeline value. Given ongoing cash burn and negligible revenue, this remains a material structural funding risk over the development period.
